children: SYDNEY--The Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Gov. Andrew Hauser again warned that inflation is too high and said a rate increase will be debated when the central bank meets at the end of the month.
In an interview with the Australian Broadcasting Corp., Hauser said he had become more concerned about inflation risks in the global economy after visiting the U.S. in recent weeks.
"The economy in Australia doing quite well...but we have one big problem, and that's inflation," he said.
Hauser also acknowledged that recent monthly inflation readings had been higher than expected.
The comments add to the RBA's increasingly hawkish tone in recent weeks, which has fueled market bets that the central bank raise interest rates further before the end of the year.

The RBA has already raised the official cash rate three times this year, reversing all the cuts it made in 2025. Still, inflation remains "too high"--something that Hauser said is making consumers and business "furious."
